findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched to {0}/{choice} syntax in a JS bundle that uses {{ }} interpolation
findings.body: All other messages in the admin-ui and account-ui property files use the i18next `{{0}}` placeholder syntax (e.g. `'{{0}}' must have maximal value of {{2}}.`). This change rewrites `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to Java MessageFormat syntax (`{0}`, `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`). If the React apps render this message via i18next, the placeholders and the choice expression will not be interpolated and users will see the literal raw string, including the `{2,choice,...}` expression. The same change was applied to `js/apps/account-ui/.../messages_en.properties` (line 188). Unless the JS apps have explicitly added MessageFormat support for this key, the server-style choice format belongs only in the Java theme bundles under `themes/`, not in the JS bundles.

findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: In the Lithuanian message bundle, `totpStep1` was changed from a Lithuanian sentence (with legitimate anchor links) to the Italian sentence 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:'. Lithuanian users will now see an Italian instruction on the TOTP setup page. The same wrong-language replacement was made for `loginTotpStep1` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (line 71). These should be proper Lithuanian translations of the new English source text.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese bundle now contains Traditional Chinese characters
findings.body: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) account bundle's `totpStep1` was changed to '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', which uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機/應用程式/安裝 instead of 手机/应用程序/安装). All other messages in this file use Simplified Chinese, so this introduces an inconsistent, wrong-script translation for mainland Chinese users.

findings.title: Locale-stripping regex character class also matches [ \\ ] ^ _
findings.body: The pattern `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties` uses the character class `[a-zA-Z-_]`, where `Z-_` is a range that also includes the characters `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, and `_`. On Windows, absolute paths contain `\` separators, so the greedy `*` can match across directory boundaries and produce a wrong English file path (e.g. consuming a backslash and parts of parent directories when a path segment contains an underscore followed by `.properties`). It would be safer to use an explicit class like `[a-zA-Z_-]` or to derive the English file name from the file name only rather than from the whole absolute path.

findings.title: Missing English reference file crashes the build with an unhelpful RuntimeException
findings.body: `verifySafeHtml()` computes the English counterpart path and opens it unconditionally; if it does not exist (e.g. a new translated properties file is added before its `_en` counterpart, or the path mapping above mis-resolves), a plain `RuntimeException("unable to read file ...")` is thrown instead of a `MojoExecutionException`. Unlike `verify()`, which wraps IO errors into `MojoExecutionException`, this escapes the mojo's error handling and aborts the build with a raw stack trace instead of a clean verification error message. The same applies to the target bundle read at line 67.
